notes: All three with-skill runs passed every assertion, while all three without-skill runs missed exactly the new behavior the edits were targeting: early codebase/context intake or anti-guessing discipline.
The development baseline still performed reasonably on client-facing clarification, but it failed on codebase discovery and proposed a default v1 scope too early.
The bug baseline centered investigation quickly, but it skipped the stronger intake step and narrowed the likely failure path before grounding expected behavior and reproduction details.

The Snyk baseline recognized the security context, but it asked for severity scope before gathering project-path and scan-intake context, which is exactly the workflow gap the rewrite was meant to close.
The skill suite adds response length and specificity rather than execution time in this eval format; the higher token count appears to buy more disciplined intake, not redundant filler.
